name: ASDS Droneship / Landing Zone
summary: Autonomous Spaceport Drone Ship (ASOG & OCISLY active, 2026 coast assignments UNVERIFIED; JRTI retired from F9 service April 21, 2026) or concrete RTLS Landing Zone (active LZ-40 at CCSFS, active LZ-4 at VSFB; historical LZ-1/LZ-2 at LC-13).
function: Provides a stabilized ocean landing deck hundreds of kilometers downrange (ASDS) or a coastal concrete pad (RTLS) for propulsive first-stage booster recovery.
materials: Modified ocean-going steel deck barge (Marmac 300-series) equipped with four GPS-guided azimuth thrusters, blast walls, and the Octagrabber recovery robot.

specs.label: LZ-1 / LZ-2 (LC-13)
specs.source: Crew-11 (Aug 1, 2025) planned final F9 LZ-1; NROL-77 (Dec 9, 2025) final F9 LZ-2; both reused for FH NROL-97 (Oct 1, 2026) — SpaceX / Spaceflight Now

specs.label: Active West Coast RTLS (LZ-4)
specs.source: VSFB former SLC-4W (active since SAOCOM 1A, Oct 8, 2018)

history: SpaceX achieved its first RTLS landing at LZ-1 on Orbcomm-2 (Dec 2015) and its first ASDS ocean landing on OCISLY during CRS-8 (April 2016). Crew-11 (Aug 1, 2025) was planned as LZ-1's final routine Falcon 9 landing and NROL-77 (Dec 9, 2025) was LZ-2's final scheduled Falcon 9 landing as East Coast RTLS shifted to LZ-40 adjacent to SLC-40; both LC-13 pads were reused on Oct 1, 2026 for Falcon Heavy NROL-97 side boosters. JRTI retired from Falcon 9 service after its final landing on April 21, 2026 and was repurposed for Starship transport. Current 2026 OCISLY/ASOG coast assignments are marked UNVERIFIED pending primary SpaceX mission-page reconciliation.
sources: SpaceX Autonomous Spaceport Drone Ship Public Specs
SpaceX / Spaceflight Now — Crew-11 (Aug 1, 2025), NROL-77 (Dec 9, 2025), NROL-97 (Oct 1, 2026)
